Strict positivity of the three edge weights proves simplicity by absolute values in the Rayleigh quotient and the eigenvector equation at a zero coordinate. In the monotone inverse-chord projective coordinate all three edge slopes are nonzero, and det(D) is twice their product. At stationarity z=Dw is nonzero and orthogonal to w. Expanding the test Rayleigh quotient cancels its constant and linear terms and gives the stated positive quadratic coefficient for small c. The remainder is cubic and both sufficiently small signs improve. Degree-zero homogeneity gives the weighted derivative identity.

Increasing a radius with both products strict keeps the off-diagonals nonpositive and increases entries, preserving PSD by comparison on absolute values. Thus positive-derivative opposite endpoints need two different incident cores, and three cores are necessary when all derivatives vanish. With the full matrix PD any radius could decrease slightly. A negative derivative exists by homogeneity unless all derivatives vanish, and in that case the stationary gain applies. Neither possibility permits an all-PD maximum.

A PD block with at least three nodes has a free internal radius whose two incident products are strict. Two-sided variation stays within the block, so a nonzero derivative or the strict stationary gain contradicts maximality. With exactly two cores the four eligible pairs give block sizes 3+3 for (0,3) and (1,4), or 2+4 for (0,4) and (1,3). For the latter pairs the checked short blocks are (5,0) and (2,3), respectively.

Each short-block transfer keeps the intervening core product fixed and leaves the other separating core unchanged. The short-block internal product decreases and its PD persists by openness. The other block sees entrywise increases with its internal products still strict. The paired first variations force both other chord derivatives positive, which together with the selected positive derivative contradicts homogeneity. Checked all four explicit exchanges.

With at least three cores, a unique singular block has size at most four and its full principal complement is PD. For size one the three proposed decreases miss its adjacent edges and affect distinct chords. For size two, decreases at 4 and 5 keep both separating edges fixed, then the A-down/B-up exchange keeps the separating core at 0 and the one at 2. For size three, B can increase within the singular block while b can decrease wholly within the complement. For size four, increases at B and t fix the derivative signs, and the simultaneous A,a-up and r,b-down exchange fixes Ar and ab while relaxing br. Openness on the whole PD complement covers any newly nonzero internal edge.

Two singular blocks contribute independent kernel vectors, giving rank at most four. Sparse reconstruction needs at least one core, preserves all maximizing endpoints and areas, and yields a full-dimensional polygon with exactly rank(L) vertices. Thus it is a triangle or quadrilateral.

For positive f, det(B)=f_1 f_2 f_3/4>0 and trace zero force precisely one positive and two negative eigenvalues. The sign of det(I-B) is the sign of 1-J. Expansion gives det(I-B)=1-(sum f_i^2+f_1 f_2 f_3)/4, so the strict witness equivalence holds at the threshold as well. The ceiling is preserved by fixed areas, and 128/279<2sqrt(3)-3 since 12*279^2-965^2=2867. The accepted incidence and strict triangle cubic facts force J<=1 for a triangle under the ceiling, so a strict maximum witness there is a quadrilateral.
